findings.title: Address validation is not bound to the connection (DNS rebinding / TOCTOU)
findings.evidence: _reject_non_public_host resolves with socket.getaddrinfo, then the fetch hands the hostname back to requests, which resolves it again independently; the IP that was checked is never pinned to the socket.
findings.recommendation: Resolve once and connect to the validated IP (e.g. mount a custom HTTPAdapter that connects to the vetted address while sending SNI/Host for the allowlisted name), or re-check the peer address after connect via response.raw._connection.sock.getpeername(). Document that the check only mitigates rebinding, and note the dependency on resolver integrity in the docstring.

findings.title: Environment proxies bypass the resolution guard
findings.evidence: requests.get is called without a Session configured with trust_env=False, so an HTTPS_PROXY/ALL_PROXY env var makes the proxy perform DNS and connect on our behalf, while _reject_non_public_host only vetted the local resolution.
findings.recommendation: Build a requests.Session with session.trust_env = False (or explicitly ignore proxies) so the connection genuinely goes to the host that was validated; if proxy support is required, treat it as an explicit opt-in with its own policy.

findings.title: DNS lookup in the guard has no timeout, so the 10s budget is not enforced
findings.evidence: socket.getaddrinfo is called with no timeout, so a slow or blackholed resolver can block safe_fetch far beyond TIMEOUT_SECONDS before requests is even started.
findings.recommendation: Bound the lookup (e.g. run it in a thread with a deadline, or use a resolver library with a configurable timeout) and surface a distinct timeout error so callers can distinguish a blocked URL from an unresolvable one.

findings.title: Security-critical module ships with no tests
findings.evidence: safe_fetch is the whole point of the change (allowlist, redirect revalidation, private-IP rejection) yet the diff adds only the module, no tests exercising the reject paths.
findings.recommendation: Add tests that monkeypatch getaddrinfo/requests.get to cover: non-https scheme, host not on allowlist, userinfo in URL, non-443 port, redirect to a non-allowlisted host, redirect to a private IP, missing Location, and exceeding MAX_REDIRECTS.
